title: sccomp: Differential Composition and Variability Analysis for Single-Cell Data
text: cellular omic data, method differential variability analysis exists, methods differential composition analysis take fundamental data properties account. introduce sccomp, generalised method differential composition variability analyses capable jointly modelling data count distribution, compositionality, group-specific variability, proportion mean-variability association, robust outliers.

title: sccomp: Differential Composition and Variability Analysis for Single-Cell Data
text: : Data modelled counts. II: Group proportions modelled compositional. III: proportion variability modelled cell-type specific. text: sccomp needs write files disk (compiled Stan models, draw files). shared servers restricted environments: Prefer installing locally – Install sccomp user-writable R library can use default cache ~/.sccomp_models. request write access – Ask system administrator permission write user directories. administrator pre-compiled models shared directory (e.g. /opt/sccomp_models), can point sccomp cache calling sccomp function. required sccomp_boxplot, sccomp_estimate, functions use internal routines check cache directory: Alternatively, pass cache_stan_model explicitly call:
code: library(sccomp)  cache_stan_model_dir <- "/opt/sccomp_models"  # Set the cache directory before any sccomp call utils::assignInNamespace("sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir", cache_stan_model_dir, ns = "sccomp")  # Now run your analysis sccomp_result <-    counts_obj |>   sccomp_estimate(formula_composition = ~ type, sample = "sample", cell_group = "cell_group",                    abundance = "count", cores = 1) |>   sccomp_test()  sccomp_result |> sccomp_boxplot(factor = "type") sccomp_result <-    counts_obj |>   sccomp_estimate(..., cache_stan_model = "/opt/sccomp_models") |>   sccomp_remove_outliers(cache_stan_model = "/opt/sccomp_models") |>   sccomp_test()  sccomp_result |> sccomp_boxplot(factor = "type", cache_stan_model = "/opt/sccomp_models")

text: individual s(pseudotime, k = 5)__* parameters sccomp_test() interpreted one--one. scientific question usually “composition differ two points (intervals) pseudotime?”. sccomp_test_smooth() answers exactly : predicts mean composition (centered log-ratio scale) two positions, forms per-draw contrast mu() - mu(), runs probability--null / FDR machinery sccomp_test() — c_effect, c_pH0 c_FDR mean thing everywhere else sccomp. linear predictor additive, covariate held constant two positions (e.g. type) cancels contrast, test isolates pseudotime effect. positive c_effect means cell group (centered log-ratio scale) abundant pseudotime 5 pseudotime 1; c_FDR controls false-discovery rate across cell groups. curve can wiggle, comparing two single points can sensitive exact positions. Fewer basis functions mean smoother curve less risk -fitting sample size modest. k = 3 yields one unpenalised linear column single wiggly basis column. code: fit_k3 <- counts_pt |>   sccomp_estimate(     formula_composition = ~ type + s(pseudotime, k = 3),     formula_variability = ~ 1,     sample              = "sample",     cell_group          = "cell_group",     abundance           = "count",     cores               = 1,     verbose             = FALSE,     max_sampling_iterations = 2000   ) pred_k3 <- fit_k3 |>   sccomp_predict(new_data = grid, number_of_draws = 200) #> Running standalone generated quantities after 1 MCMC chain, with 1 thread(s) per chain... #>  #> Chain 1  Elapsed Time: 1.22 seconds (Generated Quantities)  #> Chain 1 finished in 0.0 seconds. pred_k3 |>   filter(cell_group %in% top_cgs) |>   ggplot(aes(pseudotime, proportion_mean, colour = type, fill = type)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = proportion_lower, ymax = proportion_upper),               alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_point(data = raw, aes(y = prop, colour = type), alpha = 0.5, size = 1.2) +   facet_wrap(~ cell_group, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

what: 5. Under the hood: What s() actually decomposes into
title: Smooth (spline) terms in sccomp
text: smooth metadata used fit model stored result, can re-evaluate basis new pseudotime value. exactly sccomp_predict() internally.  top panel linear trend, bottom panel wiggly basis: columns gets one coefficient per cell group, single smoothing standard deviation sds per cell group controls much wiggle allowed. Increasing k add wiggly basis columns; penalty keep extra capacity -fitting.
code: smooth_meta    <- sccomp:::get_smooth_results(fit) smooth_specs   <- smooth_meta$smooth_specs smooth_re_objs <- smooth_meta$smooth_re_objs  grid_basis <- tibble(   pseudotime = seq(min(pt_map$pseudotime), max(pt_map$pseudotime),  length.out = 200),   type = levels(counts_obj$type)[1]  # any constant works; smooth ignores it )  basis <- sccomp:::predict_smooth_at_newdata(   smooth_specs[[1]], smooth_re_objs[[1]], grid_basis ) # Plain s() has one penalised block — for multi-penalty smooths # (e.g. bs = "fs", t2(...)) `Xr_blocks` would contain several matrices. Xr_single <- basis$Xr_blocks[[1]]  basis_long <- bind_rows(   as.data.frame(basis$Xf) |>     setNames(sprintf("lin%d", seq_len(ncol(basis$Xf)))) |>     mutate(pseudotime = grid_basis$pseudotime) |>     pivot_longer(-pseudotime, names_to = "column", values_to = "value") |>     mutate(block = "Xf  (unpenalised, joins fixed effects)"),   as.data.frame(Xr_single) |>     setNames(sprintf("basis%d", seq_len(ncol(Xr_single)))) |>     mutate(pseudotime = grid_basis$pseudotime) |>     pivot_longer(-pseudotime, names_to = "column", values_to = "value") |>     mutate(block = "Xr  (penalised, joins one RE slot, shared sds)") )  ggplot(basis_long, aes(pseudotime, value, colour = column)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +   facet_wrap(~ block, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +   labs(x = "pseudotime", y = "basis value",        title = "Decomposition of s(pseudotime, k = 5)",        subtitle = "Linear null-space (Xf) is a fixed effect; wiggly basis (Xr) is one RE slot") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

title: Clear Stan Draw Files — clear_draw_files
text: function removes Stan MCMC draw CSV files output directory. files can accumulate consume significant disk space (often GBs). Draw files created model fitting typically needed analysis session. results extracted R objects, CSV files can safely deleted.

title: Clear Stan Draw Files — clear_draw_files
code: clear_draw_files(   output_directory = "sccomp_draws_files",   older_than_days = NULL,   larger_than_mb = NULL,   pattern = "\\.csv$",   dry_run = FALSE )

title: Clear Stan Draw Files — clear_draw_files
text: output_directory character string specifying directory containing draw files. Defaults "sccomp_draws_files", default output directory used sccomp. older_than_days Numeric. specified, delete files older many days. Default NULL (delete ). larger_than_mb Numeric. specified, delete files larger size MB. Default NULL (size filter). pattern Character string. Regular expression pattern match files. Default "\.csv$" (CSV files). dry_run Logical. TRUE, report deleted without actually deleting. Default FALSE.

title: Clear Stan Draw Files — clear_draw_files
text: list invisibly containing: files_deleted: Number files deleted space_freed_mb: Approximate disk space freed MB files: Vector file paths. dry_run = TRUE, files deleted; dry_run = FALSE, files successfully deleted.

title: Clear Stan Draw Files — clear_draw_files
text: function can delete files based : files directory (default) Files older specified number days Files larger specified size MB Files matching specific pattern

title: sccomp: Differential Composition and Variability Analysis for Single-Cell Data — sccomp-package
text: Comprehensive R package differential composition variability analysis single-cell RNA sequencing, CyTOF, microbiome data. Provides robust Bayesian modeling outlier detection, random effects, advanced statistical methods cell type proportion analysis. Features include probabilistic outlier identification, mixed-effect modeling, differential variability testing, comprehensive visualization tools. Perfect cancer research, immunology, developmental biology, single-cell genomics applications. sccomp package provides comprehensive tools differential composition variability analysis single-cell RNA sequencing, CyTOF, microbiome data. implements robust Bayesian modeling outlier detection, random effects, advanced statistical methods cell type proportion analysis.

title: sccomp: Differential Composition and Variability Analysis for Single-Cell Data — sccomp-package
text: main functions : sccomp_estimate - Perform differential composition variability analysis sccomp_test - Test differential composition significance testing sccomp_remove_outliers - Identify remove outlier samples sccomp_predict - Predict cell type proportions new samples sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects - Remove unwanted variation data sccomp_proportional_fold_change - Calculate proportional fold changes Plotting functions: plot.sccomp_tbl, sccomp_boxplot, sccomp_plot_intervals_1D, sccomp_plot_intervals_2D detailed information usage, see package vignettes: browseVignettes("sccomp") software-related questions posted GitHub Issues page: https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp/issues code can viewed GitHub repository: https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp

text: Creates boxplot visualization model results sccomp. function plots estimated cell proportions across samples, highlighting significant changes cell composition according specified factor.

title: sccomp_boxplot — sccomp_boxplot
code: sccomp_boxplot(   .data,   factor,   significance_threshold = 0.05,   significance_statistic = c("pH0", "FDR"),   test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change = attr(.data,     "test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change"),   remove_unwanted_effects = FALSE,   cache_stan_model = sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir )

title: sccomp_boxplot — sccomp_boxplot
text: .data tibble containing results sccomp_estimate sccomp_test, including columns: cell_group name, sample name, read counts, factor(s), p-values, significance indicators. factor character string specifying factor interest included model stratifying boxplot. significance_threshold numeric value indicating threshold labeling significant cell-groups. Defaults 0.05. significance_statistic Character vector indicating statistic used colour significant groups. Defaults FALSE. cache_stan_model character string specifying cache directory compiled Stan models. Default sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir points ~/.sccomp_models. Use custom path restricted environments default writable.

title: Calculate Residuals Between Observed and Predicted Proportions — sccomp_calculate_residuals
text: tibble (tbl) following columns: sample - character column representing sample identifiers. cell_group - character column representing cell group identifiers. residuals - numeric column representing residuals, calculated difference observed predicted proportions. exposure - numeric column representing total counts (sum counts across cell groups) sample. residuals_unconstrained - numeric column representing residuals unconstrained scale, calculated difference inverse softmax transform observed proportions predicted unconstrained predictors.

title: Calculate Residuals Between Observed and Predicted Proportions — sccomp_calculate_residuals
text: function performs following steps: Extracts predicted mean proportions unconstrained predictors cell group sample using sccomp_predict(). Calculates observed proportions original count data. Computes residuals proportion scale subtracting predicted proportions observed proportions. Computes residuals unconstrained (log-ratio) scale : (1) applying inverse softmax (log-ratio transform sum--zero normalization) observed proportions, (2) subtracting predicted unconstrained predictors. Returns tibble containing sample, cell group, residuals (proportion scale), residuals_unconstrained (log-ratio scale), exposure (total counts per sample).

what: Plot 1D Intervals for Cell-group Effects — sccomp_plot_intervals_1D
title: Plot 1D Intervals for Cell-group Effects — sccomp_plot_intervals_1D
text: function creates series 1D interval plots cell-group effects, highlighting significant differences based given significance threshold.

title: Plot 1D Intervals for Cell-group Effects — sccomp_plot_intervals_1D
code: sccomp_plot_intervals_1D(   .data,   factor = NULL,   significance_threshold = 0.05,   test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change = attr(.data,     "test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change"),   show_fdr_message = TRUE,   significance_statistic = c("pH0", "FDR"),   sort_by = c("none", "effect", "significance", "alphabetical") )

title: Plot 1D Intervals for Cell-group Effects — sccomp_plot_intervals_1D
text: .data Data frame containing main data. factor Optional character string selecting one model factor plot. provided, plots restricted factor plus (Intercept). significance_threshold Numeric value specifying significance threshold highlighting differences. test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change positive integer. effect threshold used hypothesis test. value 0.2 correspond change cell proportion 10% cell type baseline proportion 50%. , cell type goes 45% 50%. baseline proportion closer 0 1 effect thrshold consistent value centered log-ratio uncontrained scale. show_fdr_message Logical. Whether show Bayesian FDR interpretation message plot. Default TRUE. significance_statistic Character vector indicating statistic highlight. Default "pH0". sort_by Character vector indicating sort taxa. Options "none" (default), "effect" (effect size), "significance" (FDR/pH0), "alphabetical".

what: Plot 2D Intervals for Mean-Variance Association — sccomp_plot_intervals_2D
title: Plot 2D Intervals for Mean-Variance Association — sccomp_plot_intervals_2D
text: function creates 2D interval plot mean-variance association, handling single bimodal models. highlights significant differences based given significance threshold.

title: Plot 2D Intervals for Mean-Variance Association — sccomp_plot_intervals_2D
code: sccomp_plot_intervals_2D(   .data,   factor = NULL,   significance_threshold = 0.05,   test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change = attr(.data,     "test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change"),   show_fdr_message = TRUE,   significance_statistic = c("pH0", "FDR"),   add_marginal_density = TRUE,   omit_ci = FALSE )

title: Plot 2D Intervals for Mean-Variance Association — sccomp_plot_intervals_2D
text: .data Data frame containing main data. factor Optional character string selecting one model factor plot. provided, plots restricted factor plus (Intercept). significance_threshold Numeric value specifying significance threshold highlighting differences. Default 0.05. test_composition_above_CLR_fold_change positive integer. effect threshold used hypothesis test. show_fdr_message Logical. Whether show Bayesian FDR interpretation message plot. Default TRUE. significance_statistic Character vector indicating statistic highlight. Default "pH0". add_marginal_density Logical. Whether add marginal density plots adjusted panels. Default TRUE. omit_ci Logical. Whether omit credible interval error bars. Default FALSE.

title: Plot 2D Intervals for Mean-Variance Association — sccomp_plot_intervals_2D
text: ggplot object representing 2D interval plot.

title: sccomp_predict — sccomp_predict
text: fit result sccomp_estimate. formula_composition formula. formula describing model differential abundance, example ~treatment. formula can sub-formula estimated model; case factor factored . new_data sample-wise data frame including column represent factors formula. want predict proportions 10 samples, 10 rows. Continuous covariates, including inside s() / t2(), original units fitted data. z-scored fitted samples design built. number_of_draws integer. may copies data want draw model joint posterior distribution. mcmc_seed integer. Used Markov-chain Monte Carlo reproducibility. default random number sampled 1 999999. can controlled set.seed() summary_instead_of_draws Return summary values (.e. mean quantiles) predicted proportions, return single draws. Single draws can helful better analyse uncertainty prediction. robust logical. TRUE, use robust statistics (median median absolute deviation) instead classical statistics (mean standard deviation) summary calculations.

title: sccomp_predict — sccomp_predict
text: tibble (tbl) following columns: cell_group - character column representing cell group tested. sample - factor column representing sample name predictions made. proportion_mean - numeric column representing predicted mean (median robust=TRUE) proportions model. proportion_lower - numeric column representing lower bound (2.5%) 95% credible interval predicted proportions. proportion_upper - numeric column representing upper bound (97.5%) 95% credible interval predicted proportions. unconstrained_mean - numeric column representing mean unconstrained predictors (softmax transformation). unconstrained_lower - numeric column representing lower bound (2.5%) 95% credible interval unconstrained predictors. unconstrained_upper - numeric column representing upper bound (97.5%) 95% credible interval unconstrained predictors. unconstrained - numeric column (summary_instead_of_draws=FALSE) representing individual draws unconstrained predictors. proportion - numeric column (summary_instead_of_draws=FALSE) representing individual draws predicted proportions. .draw - integer column (summary_instead_of_draws=FALSE) representing draw index.

what: Calculate Proportional Fold Change from sccomp Estimated Effects — sccomp_proportional_fold_change
title: Calculate Proportional Fold Change from sccomp Estimated Effects — sccomp_proportional_fold_change
text: function calculates proportional fold change two conditions using estimated effects sccomp model. fold changes derived model's posterior predictions rather raw counts, providing robust estimate accounts model's uncertainty covariate effects. Note! statistic descriptive used define significance - use sccomp_test() . fold changes proportions easier interpret changes centered log-ratio space, linear (proportional change different meaning rare vs abundant cell types). contrast, centered log-ratio scale used internally sccomp provides linear effects appropriate statistical inference.

title: Calculate Proportional Fold Change from sccomp Estimated Effects — sccomp_proportional_fold_change
code: sccomp_proportional_fold_change(.data, formula_composition, from, to)

title: Calculate Proportional Fold Change from sccomp Estimated Effects — sccomp_proportional_fold_change
text: .data sccomp estimate object (class 'sccomp_tbl') obtained running sccomp_estimate(). object contains fitted model estimated effects. formula_composition formula specifying model effects use calculating fold changes. match subset formula used original sccomp_estimate() call. Character string specifying reference/control condition (e.g., "benign"). Character string specifying comparison condition (e.g., "cancer").

title: Calculate Proportional Fold Change from sccomp Estimated Effects — sccomp_proportional_fold_change
text: tibble following columns: cell_group - cell group identifier proportion_fold_change - estimated fold change proportions conditions. title: sccomp_remove_outliers main — sccomp_remove_outliers
text: sccomp_remove_outliers function takes input table cell counts columns cell-group identifier, sample identifier, integer count, factors (continuous discrete). user can define linear model using input R formula, first factor factor interest. Alternatively, sccomp accepts single-cell data containers (e.g., Seurat, SingleCellExperiment, cell metadata, group-size) derives count data cell metadata.

title: sccomp_remove_outliers main — sccomp_remove_outliers
code: sccomp_remove_outliers(   .estimate,   percent_false_positive = 5,   cores = detectCores(),   inference_method = attr(.estimate, "inference_method"),   output_directory = "sccomp_draws_files",   verbose = TRUE,   mcmc_seed = sample_seed(),   max_sampling_iterations = 20000,   enable_loo = FALSE,   sig_figs = 9,   cache_stan_model = sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir,   portable = TRUE,   approximate_posterior_inference = NULL,   variational_inference = NULL,   ... )

title: sccomp_remove_outliers main — sccomp_remove_outliers
text: .estimate tibble including cell_group name column, sample name column, read counts column (optional depending input class), factor columns. percent_false_positive real number 0 100 (inclusive), used identify outliers specific false positive rate. cores Integer, number cores used parallel calculations. inference_method Character string specifying inference method use ('pathfinder', 'hmc', 'variational'). output_directory character string specifying output directory Stan draws. verbose Logical, whether print progression details. mcmc_seed Integer, used Markov-chain Monte Carlo reproducibility. default, random number sampled 1 999999. max_sampling_iterations Integer, limits maximum number iterations case large dataset used, limit computation time. enable_loo Logical, whether enable model comparison using R package LOO. useful comparing fits models, similar ANOVA. sig_figs Number significant figures use Stan model output. Default 9. cache_stan_model character string specifying cache directory compiled Stan models. sccomp version automatically appended ensure version isolation. Default sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir points ~/.sccomp_models. portable Logical, whether keep result portable caching required draws memory removing Stan draw CSV files fitting. Default TRUE save disk space move needed values memory. Set FALSE keep draw CSV files disk. approximate_posterior_inference DEPRECATED, use variational_inference argument. variational_inference DEPRECATED Logical, whether use variational Bayes posterior inference. faster convenient. Setting argument FALSE runs full Bayesian (Hamiltonian Monte Carlo) inference, slower gold standard. ... Additional arguments passed cmdstanr::sample function.

title: sccomp_remove_outliers main — sccomp_remove_outliers
text: tibble (tbl), following columns: cell_group - cell groups tested. parameter - parameter estimated design matrix described input formula_composition formula_variability. factor - covariate factor formula, applicable (e.g., present Intercept contrasts). c_lower - Lower (2.5%) quantile posterior distribution composition (c) parameter. c_effect - Mean posterior distribution composition (c) parameter. c_upper - Upper (97.5%) quantile posterior distribution composition (c) parameter. c_rhat - R-hat convergence diagnostic composition (c) parameter; values close 1.0 indicate convergence. c_ess_bulk - Bulk effective sample size composition (c) parameter; higher better. c_ess_tail - Tail effective sample size composition (c) parameter; higher better. v_lower - Lower (2.5%) quantile posterior distribution variability (v) parameter. v_effect - Mean posterior distribution variability (v) parameter. v_upper - Upper (97.5%) quantile posterior distribution variability (v) parameter. v_rhat - R-hat convergence diagnostic variability (v) parameter. v_ess_bulk - Bulk effective sample size variability (v) parameter. v_ess_tail - Tail effective sample size variability (v) parameter. Note: pH0 FDR columns computed sccomp_remove_outliers(). Run sccomp_test() result obtain hypothesis-test statistics. function also attaches several attributes result: count_data - original count data used analysis, stored attribute efficient access. model_input - model input data used fitting. formula_composition - formula used composition modeling. formula_variability - formula used variability modeling. fit - Stan fit object (pass_fit = TRUE).

what: Remove unwanted effects from a sccomp_tbl object — sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects
title: Remove unwanted effects from a sccomp_tbl object — sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects
text: method removes unwanted effects dataset using model estimates. example, fit data formula ~ factor_1 + factor_2 use formula ~ factor_1 remove unwanted variation, factor_2 effect factored .

title: Remove unwanted effects from a sccomp_tbl object — sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects
code: sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects(   .data,   formula_composition_keep = NULL,   formula_composition = NULL,   cores = detectCores() )

title: Remove unwanted effects from a sccomp_tbl object — sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects
text: .data sccomp_tbl object. result sccomp_estimate. formula_composition_keep formula. formula describing model differential abundance, example ~type. case, effect type factor preserved, factors factored . formula_composition DEPRECATED. Use formula_composition_keep instead. cores Integer, number cores used parallel calculations.

title: Remove unwanted effects from a sccomp_tbl object — sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects
text: tibble (tbl) following columns: sample - character column representing sample name data adjusted. cell_group - character column representing cell group tested. adjusted_proportion - numeric column representing adjusted proportion removing unwanted variation. adjusted_counts - numeric column representing adjusted counts removing unwanted variation. logit_residuals - numeric column representing centered log-ratio residuals calculated adjustment.

title: DEPRECATED: Remove Unwanted Variation from sccomp Estimates — sccomp_remove_unwanted_variation
text: function DEPRECATED. Please use sccomp_remove_unwanted_effects instead. function uses model remove unwanted variation dataset using estimates model. example, fit data formula ~ factor_1 + factor_2 use formula ~ factor_1 remove unwanted variation, factor_2 effect factored .

title: sccomp_scatterplot — sccomp_scatterplot
text: Creates scatterplot cell-group proportions continuous covariate, optionally overlaying posterior predictive trend fitted model. Use visualisation factor interest numeric; discrete factors prefer sccomp_boxplot().

title: sccomp_scatterplot — sccomp_scatterplot
code: sccomp_scatterplot(   .data,   factor,   significance_threshold = 0.05,   remove_unwanted_effects = FALSE )

title: sccomp_scatterplot — sccomp_scatterplot
text: .data tibble containing results sccomp_estimate sccomp_test, including columns: cell_group name, sample name, read counts, factor(s), p-values, significance indicators. factor character string specifying continuous covariate interest included model. significance_threshold numeric value indicating threshold highlighting significant cell-groups. Defaults 0.05. remove_unwanted_effects logical value indicating whether remove unwanted variation data plotting. Defaults FALSE.

title: sccomp_scatterplot — sccomp_scatterplot
text: ggplot object representing scatterplot cell proportions continuous covariate, faceted cell group.

title: sccomp_simulate — sccomp_simulate
text: Simulate counts fitted sccomp model, optionally replacing abundance coefficients mean-variability association user-chosen values. Variability taken posterior: every variability term derived abundance coefficient associated , alpha = beta * slope + intercept, plus fitted residual scatter around trend (see variability_scatter), changing abundance coefficients changes simulated variability model expects. Random effects remaining parameters come posterior draws.

title: sccomp_simulate — sccomp_simulate
code: sccomp_simulate(   fit,   formula_composition,   formula_variability = NULL,   new_data = NULL,   coefficients = NULL,   mean_dispersion_slope = NULL,   mean_dispersion_intercept = NULL,   sample = NULL,   cell_group = NULL,   variability_multiplier = 1,   number_of_draws = 1,   mcmc_seed = sample_seed(),   cores = detectCores(),   sig_figs = 9,   cache_stan_model = sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir,   variability_scatter = TRUE )

title: sccomp_simulate — sccomp_simulate
text: fit result sccomp_estimate execution. used sampling real-data properties. formula_composition formula. formula describing model differential abundance, example ~treatment. can sub-formula fitted one. formula_variability formula. formula describing model differential variability, example ~treatment. NULL, fitted variability formula used. new_data tibble including sample-specific columns (sample identifier factor columns formula). coefficients provided separately, cell_group column optional. Otherwise, include cell_group column. NULL, data used fit used. coefficients data frame/tibble cell-type specific coefficients. Must contain column matching cell_group column name every fitted cell group, columns matching design matrix column names (e.g., "(Intercept)", "typecancer"). Design columns absent set zero. design column, coefficients must sum zero across cell groups. NULL, posterior coefficients used. mean_dispersion_slope Optional slope mean-variability association. Either single number, applied every variability term, vector named variability design column (e.g. c("(Intercept)" = -0.7)), case unnamed terms keep posterior slope. NULL, posterior slopes used, 0 model fitted exclude_mean_variability_association = TRUE. mean_dispersion_intercept Optional intercept mean-variability association, forms mean_dispersion_slope. NULL, posterior intercepts used, except terms whose slope overridden, take posterior-mean intercept slope changes. sample column name character string sample identifier. NULL, one used fit. cell_group column name character string cell-group identifier. NULL, one used fit. variability_multiplier real scalar. can used artificially increasing variability simulation benchmarking purposes. number_of_draws integer. may copies data want draw model joint posterior distribution. mcmc_seed integer. Used Markov-chain Monte Carlo reproducibility. default random number sampled 1 999999. can controlled set.seed() cores Integer, number cores used parallel calculations. sig_figs Number significant figures use Stan model output. Default 9. cache_stan_model character string specifying cache directory compiled Stan models. sccomp version automatically appended ensure version isolation. Default sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir points ~/.sccomp_models. variability_scatter Logical. TRUE (default), cell group's variability drawn around mean-variability trend fitted residual standard deviation (prec_sd), fitted cell groups scatter around . FALSE, every cell group sits exactly trend.

title: sccomp_simulate — sccomp_simulate
text: rows new_data (expanded every cell group new_data cell_group column), following columns added: generated_proportions - numeric column representing generated proportions simulation. generated_counts - integer column representing generated cell counts simulation. replicate - integer column representing replicate number draw posterior distribution.

title: Default cache directory for Stan models — sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir
text: global variable defines default cache directory Stan models used sccomp package. directory used store compiled Stan models avoid recompilation subsequent runs.

code: sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir

title: Default cache directory for Stan models — sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir
text: character string containing path default cache directory.

title: Default cache directory for Stan models — sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir
text: cache directory set ~/.sccomp_models default. location used various sccomp functions store retrieve compiled Stan models, improving performance avoiding unnecessary recompilation models already compiled. Users can override default specifying different cache directory function calls accept cache_stan_model parameter.

title: Test differences along a smooth term — sccomp_test_smooth
text: smooth curve can non-linear, "difference across interval" ambiguous. Two comparison modes provided: "endpoints" (default): single values; contrast \(\mu(\code{}) - \mu(\code{})\). "average": length-2 intervals c(lo, hi); contrast average curve interval minus average interval (interval sampled resolution points). covariate varied cancels contrast centered log-ratio-scale predictor additive; therefore matter value covariates take, long held constant. factor smooths (s(x, g, bs = "fs")) -factor smooths (s(x, = g)) grouping factor selects curve tested; set via , e.g. = list(tissue = "tumor"). test mean composition: uses expected linear predictor (mu_unconstrained), overdispersed beta-binomial realisation. therefore answers "expected composition differ covariate positions?", "individual sample differ?".

title: sce_obj — sce_obj
text: Example SingleCellExperiment object containing gene expression data 106,297 cells across two assays: counts logcounts. object includes metadata assay data RNA expression, can used directly differential analysis functions like sccomp_glm.

title: sce_obj — sce_obj
text: SingleCellExperiment object following structure: assays: Two assays: counts (raw RNA counts) logcounts (log-transformed counts). rowData: additional row-level metadata present. colData: Metadata cell, including six fields: sample, type, nFeature_RNA, ident, others. dim: 1 feature 106,297 cells. colnames: Cell identifiers 106,297 cells.

title: sce_obj — sce_obj
text: SingleCellExperiment object containing single-cell RNA expression data.

title: seurat_obj — seurat_obj
